content.text: No MFN language exists anywhere in the agreement. The closest parity provisions run in our favour.

input.quote: The Licensor will make such available to the Licensee when the Licensor makes such Revisions generally available to its other licensees.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation on Licensee. Searches for MFN/"no less favourable"/best-terms/matching language returned nothing, and the fee provisions (tiered per-trade schedule at p0059-p0067, Supplemental Payments at p0078, rebates at p0076, support fees at p0086-p0089) are fixed commercial terms with no obligation for us to extend Licensor any better terms granted to third parties. The only parity-style language is p0094, under which Licensor must make Revisions available to us when it releases them generally to its other licensees — a benefit running to us, which per the detection guidance is not flagged. The Article XXII Right of First Refusal (p0139-p0141) is a change-of-control notice-and-match right, not a pricing or best-terms MFN; it is a distinct commercial term properly assessed under the ROFR/change-of-control rule rather than double-flagged here. This sits at the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), so no redline is proposed.
